Ellis — thanks for the MAP. Quick read-through and initial plan below. I sketched a lightweight evaluation timeline so your reviewers can see concrete checkpoints.

High-level: split into three parallel lanes (SOC 2 evidence intake, SIG/CAIQ delivery, DPA + retention negotiation). Each lane has an acceptance criterion and an owner.

Proposed checkpoints (week-of anchors):
- Week 1 (May 21–27): Evidence intake + control mapping (we provide control-matrix CSV, expected deliverables: control descriptions, evidence stubs, point-of-contact).
- Week 2 (May 28–June 3): SIG/CAIQ snapshot and short executive summary for your InfoSec (one-pager).
- Week 3 (June 4–10): DPA redline exchange — Redwood legal to accept small operational carveouts; major redlines to be flagged for escrow/enterprise licensing.
- Week 4 (June 11–17): Final acceptance test (test traffic in staging, retention enforcement demo, audit logging sample).

Acceptance criteria samples:
- SOC 2: access to our SOC 2 Type II report and evidence stubs for critical controls OR a plan showing SOC 2 completion date with mitigations for production gating.
- SIG: CAIQ answers with references to control artifacts + an executive risk statement.
- DPA: agreement on core terms (data processing, subprocessors, deletion windows). If DPA redline not closed, we will propose a limited SLA exception (temporary) with compensating controls.

I will own coordination. Kimberly will lead legal/DPA conversation; Marissa will run evidence intake and test staging. Can you confirm owners on your side and any hard blockers for the target dates?

Thanks,

Ellis / team — added a few clarifications from Legal:

1) DPA turnaround: our standard ask is 10 business days for first redline review. For small commercial customers we can expedite to 7 days; for enterprise carveouts we need direct SOW language and potentially an export control review.

2) Data retention variants: Hosted (default) offers 30/90/365-day retention tiers; Dedicated offers customer-configurable retention but requires a service commit and an operational runbook; Private/on-prem is defined by customer storage policies — we will supply the retention enforcement design doc.

3) SLA exception: we can consider a temporary, documented SLA deviation to allow limited production traffic before SOC 2 is finalized if the customer accepts audit-readiness milestones and compensating controls (IP allowlist, heightened logging, weekly evidence sync).

Next steps from Redwood legal: I will circulate a DPA redline (redline-dpa-priya.docx) and propose a negotiation window. We will also provide sample DPA clauses that we have accepted in similar banking customers.

—Kimberly
